summary: Solid feature with genuinely careful stream-lifecycle handling and strong tests (422 pass, 49/49 live recipe nodes pass, order book verified streaming real testnet depth and prefilling a limit order). Blocking on one item: `yarn lint:tsc` fails on this branch with TS1117 from a duplicate `UNSUPPORTED_COLLATERAL` key introduced by a merge resolution. Everything else is suggestion or nitpick.

comments.body:
This duplicates the `UNSUPPORTED_COLLATERAL` mapping already added at line 80, and it breaks the type gate:

```
$ yarn lint:tsc
ui/components/app/perps/utils/translate-perps-error.ts(80,3): error TS1117: An object literal cannot have multiple properties with the same name.
```

That is the only error `lint:tsc` reports on this branch, and `origin/main` has just one occurrence, so it came in with a merge resolution. Beyond the failing gate, this entry is dead: line 80 wins, so the specific `perpsUnsupportedCollateral` string is what actually renders and this generic `somethingWentWrong` never applies.

Deleting this line fixes both.

`recentlyViewedMarkets` is already defined at line 1336 in this same object, so this second copy is a duplicate JSON key — same merge-resolution artifact as the one in `translate-perps-error.ts`. `origin/main` has only one.

JSON.parse silently keeps the last occurrence rather than erroring, so nothing fails today, but a state-log snapshot that lists a key twice is confusing for the next person diffing controller state, and it sits out of the surrounding alphabetical ordering. Suggest deleting this block and keeping the one at 1336.

Opening the order book emits the generic `INTERACTION_TYPE.TAP`, which makes this event indistinguishable from any other tap tracked on this page — the only differentiator is the asset property, which other interactions also send.

That matters more than usual here: the feature is deliberately dark-launched (`perpsOrderBookEnabled`, production default OFF) for gradual rollout, so open-rate is exactly the signal you'll want to read during that rollout, and it can't be isolated from this event.

The surrounding code already follows the specific-value convention — `SLIPPAGE_CONFIG_OPENED` a few hundred lines below, and `CLOSE_ALL_TAPPED` / `CLOSE_ALL_CANCELLED` / `CLOSE_ALL_CONFIRMED` in `perps-view.tsx`. Worth adding an order-book-specific `INTERACTION_TYPE` value to match.

(Also: only the open transition is tracked, so open/close ratio isn't recoverable either.)

This mutates a module-level counter during the render phase (the enclosing `if (prevActivationKeyRef.current !== activationKey)` block runs in the render body, not in an effect). Render is expected to be pure, and React can invoke it more than once per commit — StrictMode double-invokes in dev, and concurrent rendering may discard a render entirely.

I traced the consequences and did not find a correctness bug: the id is stashed in `subscriptionIdRef`, so a discarded render just burns a generation number, and monotonicity — the property the guard actually relies on — still holds. So this is about purity rather than an observed defect.

If you want it airtight, allocating inside the `useLayoutEffect` that already registers the id (keying the effect on `activationKey`) would move the side effect out of render without changing the guarantee.

`ORDER_BOOK_DISPLAY_LEVELS` is only ever used as `groupOrderBook`'s default parameter at line 201, and every call site passes `ORDER_BOOK_AGGREGATED_LEVELS` explicitly (`order-book.tsx:350`) — so neither the export nor the default is reachable.

It looks like a leftover from the client-side-aggregation approach that the server-side `nSigFigs`/`mantissa` path replaced. Since the two constants mean different things (subscribed slippage-book depth vs the 5-level fast-mode ladder), leaving both exported invites picking the wrong one later. Suggest dropping it and making `maxLevels` required.

`aria-controls` points at `configModalId`, but `PerpsOrderBookConfigModal` returns `null` while closed, so this references an element id that isn't in the DOM for the entire time the trigger is collapsed — which is most of the time.

The rest of the ARIA here is right (`aria-haspopup="dialog"` plus `aria-expanded` already convey the relationship), so the simplest fix is to make it conditional: `{...(isConfigOpen && { 'aria-controls': configModalId })}`.
